what: OneMain Holdings lends money to people with imperfect credit. It makes personal instalment loans of a few thousand dollars, typically secured against a car or unsecured, repaid in fixed monthly amounts, arranged in branches and online. It also sells credit cards and insurance products alongside the loans.
customers: American households whose credit scores put them below prime bank lending standards but who have steady income. A large share of customers visit a branch and speak to a person.
money: Interest on instalment loans, the core business.
Credit insurance and protection products sold with loans, plus credit card interest.
moat: A branch network of over a thousand offices is an unusual asset in consumer lending: meeting a borrower in person improves underwriting on customers whose credit files are thin, and it gives OneMain a channel competitors relying on digital marketing cannot match. Decades of loan performance data inform its credit models.
risks: Credit losses are the central risk. These are borrowers with limited savings, so a rise in unemployment feeds through to defaults quickly.
Reported debt of about $22.8B funds the loan book, but it must be refinanced continually, and funding costs rise when credit markets tighten.
Regulatory attention to high-interest consumer lending is persistent, and a federal or state cap on rates or on insurance products sold with loans would alter the economics.
Competition from digital lenders and from buy-now-pay-later products targets the same customers with lower acquisition costs.
The shares trade at about 8.5 times earnings, which is the market's way of saying it doubts the earnings are durable.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $4.0B in 2021 to $4.9B in 2025.
The shares pay a substantial dividend, and net income of about $767.0M against a $6.4B market value is a high earnings yield.
Loan yields are high enough to absorb significant credit losses and still earn a profit, which is the business model rather than an accident.
Fourteen analysts average a $66.86 target, about 20% above the current price.
watch: Net charge-off rate on the loan book. In subprime lending, the loss rate decides everything, and it is reported monthly, so it gives early warning long before earnings do.
